newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close lower ahead of CPI release.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close lower ahead of CPI release.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed lower on Thursday in thin trading as investors awaited the release of the February consumer price index on Friday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.07 pct to 103.72
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct at 102.93
Volume was very low at 115 million shekels.

"The market was extremely quiet today because we're all waiting for the CPI release. CPI-linked bonds made a very big move and they have to rest until there is more information on the inflation figure," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.

"Inflation-linked bonds cannot rise any further because there is much uncertainty concerning the CPI. Most analysts believe that it will show a 1.1-1.2 percent rise for February, but others predict a rise of only 0.8 percent," said Miri Dagan of Clal Insurance.
Dealers said unlinked bonds traded quietly. Dagan said the Makam closed almost unchanged on very low volume of only 20 million shekels.
Dollar-linked bonds closed lower after the shekel rose against the dollar. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3650 shekels against 3.3730 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
